Emily — thanks for the matrix and the clear questions. Below is a concise Q&A + an operational proposal we can include in the SOW. I'll also attach a high-level workflow diagram.

1) Phased erasure pattern (recommended):
   - Phase 0 (Immediate): Customer-initiated account/object delete triggers token-level redaction for any stored PHI fields in the active index + immediate removal from user-facing datasets. We aim for a 24–72h surface-delete window for hosted API requests depending on tier.
   - Phase 1 (Soft retention): Non-PHI metadata required for billing/compliance (invoice id, transaction timestamps) is moved to an isolated retention store with access controls and immutable retention tags. This store resides in the requested residency region. Retention TTLs are configurable per-account; default templates include a 7-year template for financial metadata.
   - Phase 2 (Final erase): After retention TTL expires (or on customer-directed final purge), records in the retention store are cryptographically shredded and indexes are compacted. Audit log entries persist in tamper-evident logs (hash-chained) but can be pseudonymized if requested.

2) Caches and KV state:
   - Live inference KV caches: ephemeral in-GPU or in-memory caches are zeroed on delete events during the Phase 0 operation. For customer isolation, we route KV caches per-tenant; we do not persist raw user PHI in long-lived KV snapshots.
   - Tiered caches (edge / CDN): we honor cache-control headers and TTLs; we provide purge APIs and integrate with CDN invalidation when required.

3) Backups and replicas:
   - Operational backups: nightly backups are retained per policy in the specified region. If a delete request arrives, we first mark the object as deleted and schedule a targeted purge from the next backup cycle; we offer an expedited backup purge option for DPA/SOWs which reduces purge latency to the next backup window plus a processing window (typically 48–96h).

4) Residency for logs and backups:
   - By default, backups and audit logs are stored in-region (US or EU) per account. We can provide a private bucket option for enterprise (bring-your-own-bucket) and KMS key ownership for the retention store.

5) E-discovery and legal holds:
   - We support hold flags at the tenant or object level. When a hold is active, final erasure is deferred; we provide an export and chain-of-custody report.

Next steps:
- If this matches your needs we can produce a short mutual action plan with timelines (expedited purge add-on, retention TTLs, hold procedures).

Soojin / Marissa — quick technical notes to call out for the SOW:
- Snapshot cadence: our cold backups are incremental with a 30-day retention index for deltas; full-image purge of a deleted object may require reconstruction across shards — that's why expedited purge has a 48–96h window.
- Model cache persistence: we do not persist user PHI in trained model weights; only transient KV is possible. However, prompt/response logs used for debugging are stored in the observability plane and must be scoped and purged per the policy above.
- Audit logs: we can provide hashed audit entries and, if required, a pseudonymization layer to store hashes instead of clear identifiers.

I'll add a short appendix for the engineering implementation details for the SOW.

— Karthik

Thanks — that helps. A few clarifications from legal and compliance:
- Acme requires: immediate user-facing deletion within 24 hours for PHI; final scheduled purge may be allowed to respect fiscal/legal retention up to 7 years for Billing IDs.
- For backups: legal needs an SLA for expedited purge and a certification process (we'll want a written attestation that the targeted backup objects were removed).
- Holds: when a legal hold is placed, we need a clear API and logging to show hold start/end and the scope.

Can you include a sample mutual action plan with milestones and the expedited-purge add-on cost? Procurement requested that before they route to contract.

Emily

Mutual action plan (draft):
- Day 0: Contract signature & account provisioning; configure region and retention templates (owner: Acme / Redwood ops).
- Day 1–3: Activate retention tags and demo purge workflow on staging tenant (owner: Redwood solutions engineer).
- Day 4–7: Run a simulated delete -> backup purge (expedited) and provide attestation report (owner: Redwood compliance).
- Ongoing: Weekly sync for 30 days post-cutover; legal-hold dashboard access provided to Acme compliance.

SLA notes:
- Surface delete (Phase 0): target 24h for hosted API default; 24h is achievable for Enterprise with dedicated capacity commit.
- Expedited backup purge: 48–96h window; add-on pricing listed in attached cost sheet.
